raw_response:
I am 73 years old this year. I have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I only finished primary school, but I know every corner of my land. I farm alone now, so every bag of fertilizer I have to carry myself, and every yuan I spend comes out of my own pocket. I have a well, so when the sky does not give rain, I can pump water.

This year I will keep my 2 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 1 mu in cotton. I thought about dropping the cotton because bending down to pick it hurts my old back, but my neighbor Lao Wang got a good price for cotton last year, and I know how to grow it. With only 3 mu, I cannot afford to take big risks, so I do what worked before.

For the wheat: I sowed it last October on 2 mu with improved seeds, about 35 jin per mu, the same variety as last year from the shop in town. Before sowing I spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. The bag has three numbers on it — I think 15-15-15 or something close. That is my base dressing. In March, at green-up, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, and another half bag at jointing stage. Urea is 46% nitrogen, the dealer told me that years ago. So with the compound and urea together, I figure about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, and 7 kg of phosphorus and 6 kg of potassium. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. I spray twice for aphids and rust. Last year I got 450 kg per mu, and I expect about the same this year if the weather is normal.

For the maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize on the same 2 mu. I do not till much — I just drill the seeds into the wheat stubble to save time, because the rainy season is coming and I need the maize in the ground fast. I put compound fertilizer in the row at sowing, about 40 kg per mu, then at big trumpet stage I spread 20 kg of urea per mu. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times — after sowing if it is dry, at big trumpet, and at filling. Two sprays for corn borers and armyworm. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

For the cotton: I plant 1 mu in late April. I use improved cotton seeds. Before planting I spread 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, and at flowering I add 10 kg of urea per mu. That gives about 12 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain — I spray four times for bollworm and whitefly. I irrigate three times. I hope for 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Money is tight on a 3 mu farm. A 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer costs about 150 yuan, and urea is about 120 yuan. My fertilizer bill for the whole year is around 1,500 yuan, plus seeds and pesticide. But I learned long ago that it is better to waste a little fertilizer than to lose yield. A bad harvest means disaster; an extra half bag of urea is just a cost. So I will not cut back this year. If anything, I might add a little more urea to the wheat because last year the lower leaves turned yellow early.
